Case Study: Diabetic Nephropathy Meta-Analysis

Source: vignettes/case-diabetic-nephropathy.Rmd
case-diabetic-nephropathy.Rmd

This vignette demonstrates a comprehensive meta-analysis workflow for diabetic nephropathy (DN) gene expression datasets. We show how to systematically search, filter, annotate, and visualize relevant GEO datasets to prepare for downstream meta-analysis.

Introduction

Diabetic nephropathy is a major complication of diabetes and a leading cause of chronic kidney disease. Conducting a meta-analysis of gene expression studies can help identify robust molecular signatures. This workflow demonstrates how to use geokit to:

  • Search GEO using multiple query strategies
  • Build a customized metadata database
  • Filter datasets by quality criteria
  • Visualize dataset characteristics
  • Prepare a curated list for downstream analysis
library(geokit)
library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)

1. Multi-Strategy Dataset Discovery

Different researchers use varying terminology, so we query for both “diabetic nephropathy” and “diabetic kidney disease” and merge the results.

dn_search_terms <- c(
  "diabetic nephropathy[ALL] AND Homo sapiens[ORGN] AND GSE[ETYP]",
  "diabetic kidney disease[ALL] AND Homo sapiens[ORGN] AND GSE[ETYP]"
)

dn_gse_list <- lapply(dn_search_terms, geo_search)
#> → Parsing GEO records
#> → Parsing GEO records
dn_gse <- unique(dplyr::bind_rows(dn_gse_list))

cat(sprintf("Found %d unique GSE datasets\n", nrow(dn_gse)))
#> Found 133 unique GSE datasets
head(dn_gse[, 1:3])

2. Extract Sample Information

Extract the number of samples from the Contains field to enable filtering by sample size. This count covers every sample in a series regardless of group — cases, controls, and technical replicates — so treat it as an upper bound; group sizes and balance must be verified from sample annotations before a dataset is included in a meta-analysis.

dn_gse <- dn_gse |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    number_of_samples = str_match(
      Contains, "(\\d+) Samples?"
    )[, 2L, drop = TRUE],
    number_of_samples = as.integer(number_of_samples)
  )

summary(dn_gse$number_of_samples)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.     NAs 
#>    1.00    8.00   18.00   41.77   40.25  616.00       1

3. Filter by Quality Criteria

Apply filters for sample size and study type to focus on candidate expression profiling studies. Note that this filter admits both microarray and RNA-seq records (“expression profiling by high throughput sequencing”); intensity- and count-based studies cannot be pooled directly, so process them separately or tighten the filter to arrays for a single integrated analysis.

dn_gse_filtered <- dn_gse |>
  dplyr::filter(
    # At least 6 samples for meaningful analysis
    number_of_samples >= 6,
    # Focus on expression profiling studies
    str_detect(Type, regex("expression profiling", ignore_case = TRUE)),
    # Exclude methylation studies (defensive: no current GEO Type string
    # passes the filters above, but this guards against future variants)
    !str_detect(Type, regex("methylation", ignore_case = TRUE)),
    # Exclude compound SuperSeries so each study has a single assay type
    !str_detect(Type, ";")
  )

cat(sprintf(
  "After filtering: %d datasets (%.1f%% of original)\n",
  nrow(dn_gse_filtered),
  100 * nrow(dn_gse_filtered) / nrow(dn_gse)
))
#> After filtering: 89 datasets (66.9% of original)

4. Build a Metadata Database

Fetch detailed metadata for the filtered datasets using geo_meta(). This creates a local database for offline analysis and detailed inspection. The download may take several minutes depending on the number of datasets; if you have an NCBI API key, set it as the ENTREZ_KEY environment variable to speed up searching.

dn_metadb_dir <- "dn_metadb"
dir.create(dn_metadb_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

dn_metadb <- geo_meta(
  dn_gse_filtered[["Series Accession"]],
  odir = dn_metadb_dir
)

# Save for future use
saveRDS(dn_metadb, file.path(dn_metadb_dir, "dn_metadb.rds"))

In a later session, reload the saved database and calculate the actual sample counts from the sample identifier list:

dn_metadb <- readRDS(file.path(dn_metadb_dir, "dn_metadb.rds"))

dn_metadb <- dn_metadb |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    number_of_samples = lengths(
      strsplit(Series_sample_id, "; ", fixed = TRUE)
    )
  )

5. Annotate and Categorize Datasets

Categorize datasets by criteria relevant to diabetic nephropathy research, searching the title, summary, and overall design fields of each series. These keyword assignments are screening heuristics only — inspect each candidate’s design and sample annotations (tissue, cell type, group definitions) before final inclusion, as keyword matches can also pick up cell-line or animal studies.

dn_metadb <- dn_metadb |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    search_text = paste(Series_title, Series_summary, Series_overall_design),
    has_nephropathy = str_detect(
      search_text, regex("nephropath", ignore_case = TRUE)
    ),
    has_kidney = str_detect(
      search_text, regex("kidney|renal", ignore_case = TRUE)
    ),
    tissue_type = dplyr::case_when(
      str_detect(search_text, regex("glomerul", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~
        "glomerular",
      str_detect(search_text, regex("tubul", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "tubular",
      str_detect(search_text, regex("kidney|renal", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~
        "kidney",
      TRUE ~ "other"
    )
  )

table(dn_metadb$tissue_type)

6. Visualization: Dataset Characteristics

Timeline of Dataset Submissions

GSE accession numbers are assigned chronologically, so they can serve as a time proxy for when studies were submitted. Depending on the records, the SOFT metadata may also provide explicit dates (e.g., Series_submission_date) that you can parse instead.

dn_metadb <- dn_metadb |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    gse_number = as.integer(str_extract(Series_geo_accession, "\\d+"))
  )

ggplot(dn_metadb, aes(x = gse_number)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of DN Datasets by GEO Accession Number",
    subtitle = "GSE numbers are assigned chronologically (lower = older)",
    x = "GSE Number",
    y = "Number of Datasets"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 9),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

Sample Size Distribution 

ggplot(dn_metadb, aes(x = number_of_samples)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "coral", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = median(dn_metadb$number_of_samples, na.rm = TRUE),
    linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Sample Sizes in DN Datasets",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Median: %s samples",
      format(median(dn_metadb$number_of_samples, na.rm = TRUE))
    ),
    x = "Number of Samples",
    y = "Number of Datasets"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

Platform Usage Trends 

platform_summary <- dn_metadb |>
  dplyr::count(Series_platform_id, sort = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(n, n = 10)

ggplot(platform_summary, aes(x = reorder(Series_platform_id, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkgreen", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.5) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Platforms Used in DN Studies",
    x = "Platform ID",
    y = "Number of Studies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )

7. Prepare a Curated Dataset List

Create a final curated list of datasets suitable for meta-analysis.

dn_curated <- dn_metadb |>
  dplyr::filter(
    number_of_samples >= 10,
    has_nephropathy | has_kidney
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(desc(number_of_samples)) |>
  dplyr::select(
    Series_geo_accession,
    Series_title,
    number_of_samples,
    Series_platform_id,
    tissue_type
  )

head(dn_curated, 10)

write.csv(
  dn_curated,
  file.path(dn_metadb_dir, "dn_curated_datasets.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

8. Next Steps for Meta-Analysis

With this curated list, you can proceed to:

  1. Download expression data: Use geo_matrix() to download series matrix files
  2. Quality control: Examine sample annotations and expression distributions
  3. Data integration: Normalize and batch-correct across studies
  4. Differential expression: Identify genes consistently dysregulated in DN
  5. Pathway analysis: Investigate enriched biological processes
top_gse <- dn_curated$Series_geo_accession[1]
eset <- geo_matrix(top_gse, odir = tempdir())

print(eset)
dim(Biobase::exprs(eset))

Instead of manually inspecting the curated list, you can also hand it to an LLM for interactive exploration with geo_chat(); see vignette("geo-chat") for details.

chat <- geo_chat(
  NULL,
  dn_curated,
  data_description = paste(
    "Curated diabetic nephropathy GEO Series selected for meta-analysis.",
    "number_of_samples is counted from the SOFT sample list."
  )
)
chat$app()

Summary

This workflow demonstrated how to:

  • Use multiple search strategies to comprehensively identify relevant datasets
  • Build a customized metadata database with geo_meta()
  • Apply quality filters for sample size and study type
  • Visualize dataset characteristics over time
  • Prepare a curated list for downstream meta-analysis

The systematic approach supports reproducibility and helps identify the most suitable datasets for gene expression meta-analysis in diabetic nephropathy research.
